name: AOI06 Palmeira, Mozambique

method.name: lightgbm
method.summary: LightGBM classifier on 14 radar features (HH, HV, HV minus HH, the change between dates, and 5x5 local mean and spread), each with the area's median over land with no water on record (JRC 0%) removed; flood where the probability is at least 0.36; not water on 5 Jan (DSWx-S1); not permanent water (JRC occurrence >= 50%).

aoi05_test.decision_rule: higher AOI05 IoU at 3 decimals wins; a tie keeps the rule

post_fix_rerun.label: post-fix rerun
post_fix_rerun.note: Not a clean test. The land-median fix was found on AOI01 after AOI05 had been used as the test. The clean held-out figure is the v1 score in test_lgbm_vs_rule.json.
post_fix_rerun.decided_before_scoring: The fix stays whatever this number is. The method choice is reopened only if LightGBM falls below the tuned rule's AOI05 IoU of 0.521 (at 3 decimals).

legend.2: #bdbdbd at alpha 170: valid, outside the Copernicus mapped area
legend.3: #e6ab02 at alpha 170: unclear: HH rose, possible flooded vegetation
legend.4: #7570b3 at alpha 170: edge buffer, not scored

limits: NISAR Beta data: not fully calibrated. The 17 Jan scene is about 3 dB brighter overall, so each area's median over land with no water on record (JRC 0%) is removed before the classifier sees it.
Agreement with Copernicus, not accuracy: the reference is a Sentinel-1 (C-band) map made 23 minutes before the NISAR pass, not ground truth.
AOI06 is the training area: the method's settings were chosen here, so its agreement figure is in-sample, not a test. The held-out test is AOI05.
Pixels where HH rose by more than 3 dB (possible flooded vegetation) are not scored. This method only finds open water.
Permanent water (JRC occurrence >= 50%) is never counted as flood.
A 2-pixel band along the Copernicus mapped-area edge is not scored. Flood polygon edges are scored.
The classifier learned from the Copernicus map of AOI06 only.
NISAR frame 165 covers only part of this grid: 35% has no NISAR data on at least one of the two dates.

On the held-out area AOI05, the tuned rule scored IoU 0.521 and LightGBM 0.572 against Copernicus, so the LightGBM classifier is used. That is the one clean test. A fix to how the land median is taken was found later, on AOI01, and AOI05 was scored once more after it (a post-fix rerun, not a clean test): IoU 0.574.
Against this area's reference, the tuned rule scores IoU 0.558 and LightGBM 0.577 (both in-sample).
714 ha (6%) of the detected new water was already dark in NISAR's 5 Jan image. DSWx-S1 (or JRC) called it dry, so it counts as new, but some of it may have been water before 17 Jan.

Buildings: 5 OpenStreetMap buildings sit inside detected new water, out of 18,515 mapped on this grid. The count can be too high or too low. Too low: OpenStreetMap is incomplete here, and flooded built-up areas look bright in radar, so open-water detection misses them. Too high: a 30 m pixel is larger than a house, so a building beside water can fall on a water pixel, and some detected water may not be flood. It says nothing about damage. Data: OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL.
